title: Criteria Tell You More than Ratings: Criteria Preference-Aware Light Graph Convolution for Effective Multi-Criteria Recommendation

problem.claim: Multi-criteria recommendation systems need to leverage criteria-level rating information.

gap.claim: How to design multi-criteria recommender systems with graph neural networks remains unexplored.

contributions.claim: A criteria preference-aware light graph convolution method, CPA-LGC, captures user criteria preferences and collaborative signals in high-order graph connections.
An MC expansion graph transforms user-item multi-criteria ratings into an expanded bipartite graph.
CPA-LGC introduces user-specific criteria-preference embeddings and item-specific criterion embeddings into graph convolution.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe this work as the first attempt to design a GNN-aided multi-criteria recommender system.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Evaluations on four real-world datasets report superiority over benchmark multi-criteria and GNN-based recommendation methods.
The evaluations report effectiveness of CPA-LGC's core components.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multi-criteria recommendation is used across e-commerce applications.
GNN-based multi-criteria recommendation design is identified as unexplored.
The work proposes CPA-LGC and an MC expansion graph with criteria-aware embeddings.
The method is evaluated on four real-world datasets for comparative performance, component effectiveness, and efficiency.

source_observation.claim: The method represents multi-criteria ratings as an expanded graph and adds user- and item-specific criteria representations.

interpretation.claim: Preserving structured preference dimensions may improve graph-based recommendation beyond treating ratings as undifferentiated interactions.

application.claim: For multi-attribute recommendation problems, model attribute-specific user and item representations alongside collaborative connectivity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when this modeling approach may fail or underperform.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the four datasets, evaluation metrics, or exact performance gains.
The abstract does not describe the benchmark implementations or computational-efficiency measurements.
The abstract does not provide ablation details or reproducibility information.
